data.ruling: The refutation stands on both of its grounds. The claim says the order of grounds is (1) the 2.0 x 1.6 mm case, (2) maker status read or not read, (3) a Digi-Key second vendor or an alternate only, (4) body size and height, (5) JLCPCB stock margin. The ranking does not follow that order. (a) ETQP3M3R3KVP ties the Coilcraft 4 x 4 mm parts on ground 1, because none of them is 2.0 x 1.6 mm. It also ties them on ground 2, because the claim itself lists both Panasonic and Coilcraft as not read. On ground 3 it wins: Digi-Key lists it as Active with stock, and Digi-Key does not list XGL4020-332MEC, XFL4020-332MEC, XAL4030-332MEC or XEL4030-332MEC. By the stated order it ranks above all four, yet it ranks last (rank 8), and its reason leads with body size, which is ground 4. (b) XFL4020-332MEC ties XAL4030-332MEC and XEL4030-332MEC on grounds 1 to 3: all are Coilcraft 4 x 4 mm parts, none has a maker status read, and none is on Digi-Key. On ground 4 XFL4020 is the lower part, 2.10 mm max against 3.1 mm max, yet it ranks below both. Its reason cites DCR (direct-current resistance) and Coilcraft's pointer to XGL4020. Neither is a stated ground, and the pointer is not a lifecycle status. Rank 1 (AOTA-B201610S3R3-101-T) is not affected. Scope is function: the finding concerns the ranking basis this function reports, not any one part. Limit of this reading: the FU-A2 re-rank return is not on disk, neither under results nor in scratch/FU-A2, so the ranks 7 and 8 and their reason texts are taken from the verifier's account. They match the pattern of the FU-A1 re-rank (results/.../FU-A1/006-rerank-R1.json), which puts ETQP3M3R3KVP last with body size as its first reason and XFL4020 below XAL4030 and XEL4030 on DCR.
